title: Sensex, Nifty pause for breath; Realty surges as rupee slips on dollar buying - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Sectorally, Realty led with gains of around 4.5%, followed by Media at 2.46%, Insurance at 2.90%, and PSU Banks at 1.51%.

Benchmark indices marked time on Thursday, holding on to marginal gains as the nine-session rally ran into profit-booking at elevated levels, even as the broader market continued to outperform. The day’s most striking move came from the Realty sector, which surged around 4.5 per cent, while the rupee briefly touched a six-month high before retreating sharply.

The BSE Sensex closed at 81,911.01, up 31.61 points or 0.04 per cent, after trading in a range of 81,576.15 to 82,325.61. The NSE Nifty 50 settled at 25,299.35, gaining 44.30 points or 0.18 per cent. Bank Nifty was the standout, closing at 61,518.50, up 726.10 points or 1.19 per cent, marking its eighth consecutive session of gains. Broader markets outperformed the benchmarks, with the Nifty Midcap 100 rising around 0.85 per cent and the Nifty Smallcap 100 advancing approximately 1.12 per cent.

”After the recent sharp rally, some consolidation and sectoral rotation appear healthy,” said Ajit Mishra, SVP – Research at Religare Broking, capturing the mood of a session that saw bulls and bears reach a truce near recent highs.

Sectorally, Realty led with gains of around 4.5 per cent, followed by Media at 2.46 per cent, Insurance at 2.90 per cent, and PSU Banks at 1.51 per cent. On the other side, Auto fell over 1 per cent, FMCG dropped 0.74 per cent, and IT slipped 0.41 per cent — its fourth consecutive session of decline.

Among Nifty 50 stocks, HDFC Life led gainers at 3.91 per cent to ₹596, followed by Shriram Finance at 3.51 per cent to ₹1,003.15, Bajaj Finance at 3.06 per cent to ₹1,111.80, SBI Life at 2.61 per cent to ₹1,813.20, and Bajaj Finserv at 2.27 per cent to ₹1,886.90. Mahindra & Mahindra was the top loser, falling 2.51 per cent to ₹3,378, with Nestlé India down 2.11 per cent to ₹1,260.80, Maruti Suzuki declining 1.84 per cent to ₹12,942, Hindustan Unilever dropping 1.44 per cent to ₹1,974.50, and TMPV down 1.42 per cent to ₹295.

The rupee had a choppy session, touching a six-month high of 93.62 against the US dollar before aggressive dollar demand from a state-owned bank, ahead of the inflation data release, pushed USD/INR back above 94.00. ”Going forward, spot USD/INR support is seen at 93.50, while resistance is likely around 94.30,” said Dilip Parmar, Senior Research Analyst at HDFC Securities. Brent crude held near $92 a barrel, offering macro support, while WTI traded in the $86–87 range.

FIIs bought equities worth approximately ₹12,563 crore in the previous session, taking their cumulative November inflows to around $6.43 billion. DIIs remained net sellers for a ninth straight session.

“The market’s next directional cue will likely come from the October CPI release, due after market hours,” noted Ponmudi R, CEO of Enrich Money, adding that a hotter-than-expected print could introduce fresh volatility into Friday’s session, particularly for rate-sensitive sectors. Friday also brings Q2FY27 results from Grasim Industries, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles, ABB India, Eicher Motors and Godrej group companies, giving investors fresh earnings data to assess whether the rally has fundamental backing beyond FII flows.
